cases.description: A newly created Position has no exit trade; getExit() should return null.
After the position is closed (e.g., by calling operate(...) that creates an exit Trade), getExit() must return the stored exit Trade object.
A Position that has only an entry Trade (opened but not yet closed) should still return null for getExit(). The exit is only set after the position is closed.

After the Position is closed (operate(...) creates the exit Trade), subsequent calls to getExit() must return the exact same Trade object (reference equality). This verifies that the exit reference is stored and not recreated.

Calling operate(...) on a Position that is already closed must not replace the existing exit Trade. After the first close, capture the exit Trade, invoke operate() again with a later index, and verify getExit() still returns the original Trade instance.
When a closed Position is serialized and then deserialized, getExit() should still return the stored exit Trade (i.e., the exit survives the serialization process).
